title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR 5 open — deny that meriting just condemnation = truly/properly sinned
pass_a_gloss: GAR 5 denies the hinge Placeus used: that meriting just condemnation means one truly and properly sinned. Properly may mean only in one's own person, by one's own—not another's—sin.
pass_b_english: GAR. 5. That is denied on which the learned man builds his whole reason, that those who have so sinned that they have merited just condemnation have truly and properly sinned. What if to sin truly and properly is to sin in one's own person, and to offend by one's own, not by another's, sin? For one's own is opposed to another's.
source_text: GAR. 5. Negatur illud, cui totam suam rationem superstruit Vir doctus, Qui peccarunt, ita ut iustam condemnationem meriti sint, eos vere & proprie peccasse. Quid si vere & proprie peccare est in propria sua persona peccare, & suo non alieno peccato delinquere? Proprium enim alieno opponitur.

lemmas.gloss: to have truly and properly sinned

choices.choice: Deny hinge: meriting condemnation ≠ truly/properly (personal) sin
